correctness.rationale: For every fourteen-coordinate distribution D of total weight <=6, the exact acyclic recursion R(D)=supp(D) union over all legal first moves of R(D-2e_u+e_v) enumerates exactly the reachable targets because each move reduces total weight by one. Two independent programs, one implementing this dynamic program on cyclic Fano incidence and one doing literal breadth-first state search on the nonzero binary-vector model, find zero solvable initial states below weight six and 161 at weight six. The three disjoint geometric classes count 98+21+42=161; both independent tests verify equivalence of geometry and solvability. The enumerated one-unit exchanges give 42 edges, 21 P3 and 98 isolates, including the nonlocal comparison. A third finite program verifies a complete 38,760-state reachability certificate and 336 automorphisms yielding orbit sizes 21,42,42,56. Computation is exhaustive for this fixed finite domain and does not assert an infinite-family result.

value.rationale: Optimal pebbling is a motivated resource-placement extremum: the smallest total stock that can individually reach any target under lossy transport. On the canonical Fano-plane incidence graph, the theorem classifies every optimum by incidence geometry, explains four automorphism classes, and reveals an unexpectedly fragmented optimal-allocation space: exactly 21 mobile triples versus 98 configurations frozen even under nonlocal single-pebble relocation. Such precise class and mobility information is not a routine consequence of the general pebbling upper bound or of the minimum number alone. The result is intentionally finite and self-contained.
